doc.title: Joe Wilder Part 2 interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, October 12, 1998

title: Recording 'The Pretty Sound' for Columbia
summary: His first major-label album under his own name, promoted by Nat Shapiro, recorded in a single day in January 1959, with Rowe reading praise from the liner notes.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: My first record date: sessions, personnel, discography

blocks.x: When was the first opportunity to get with a major label, under your own name?

That was when I did an album called “The Pretty Sound” for Columbia. And Nat Shapiro, that’s who — I couldn’t think of Nat’s name — he’s the one who promoted me, I mean for that record and for “Peter Gunn.” He was responsible for that. But that was the first time. I did some things for Savoy, but nothing, as far as I’m concerned, of the quality of the Columbia things.
Well I noticed in looking, this was recorded it says January 18, 1959. So you had one day to do ten songs.
We did the whole thing in one session, that’s right.
It took us probably two sessions involved, but it was the same day.
Right. They do three hour sessions? That’s what I’ve been hearing from other folks.
And they like you to avoid the overtime, don’t they?
Well you said you hadn’t read these liner notes —

— and I just wanted to — I could read anything and you wouldn’t know it. It says, “Joe Wilder is blessed with impeccable taste, penetrating intelligence and the most beautiful horn tone since the great Joe Smith blew his heavenly sounds in Fletcher Henderson’s band.”
Isn’t that nice? “British critics said he’s one of the very few completely fresh and original trumpet stylists to emerge with modern jazz.” Not bad.
So I’m out today to find out the secret of Joe Wilder’s tone, so I can sell the information.
